description: Certificate validation bypass in Node.js https.Agent via cross-policy TLS session reuse
overview: A certificate validation bypass in Node.js `https.Agent` lets a cached TLS session authenticated under one CA policy be reused by a later request with a stricter policy. `https.Agent.prototype.getName()` assigns the same Agent and session-cache key to a request that omits `ca` and one that explicitly supplies `ca: []`, because an omitted value appends nothing to the key while an empty array stringifies to an empty string. The two policies differ: omitting `ca` uses the default trust store, while supplying `ca` replaces it. Since they share a key, a TLS session authenticated under the broader default policy is handed to a new connection made under the later `ca: []` policy, and TLS 1.3 session resumption carries the earlier authentication forward, so the second request reports `authorized === true` and transmits confidential data to a server its own CA policy would reject on a fresh connection. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
